manifest.author: Human Not Found
manifest.description: Rules for who speaks next in a group discussion (speaker picks next, raise hands, least active next), and a participation measure that leaves moderators out.

about.summary: The turn-taking rules of everyday conversation: the speaker picks who goes next; otherwise anyone may take the floor; otherwise the speaker goes on.
about.how_it_works: Follows Sacks, Schegloff and Jefferson (1974). The first group member in the list speaks first. After each message the speaker names the next speaker (turn.pass), who is invited. If the speaker answers 'anyone', every other participant is asked privately whether they want to speak (turn.request) and the first to say yes gets the floor. If nobody wants it, the previous speaker continues; after the configured number of such quiet rounds in a row the step ends. Moderators (role 'moderator') are never the first speaker and are left out of the counts; after each group member's message they are asked first whether they want to step in, and a speaker may also name them. After each turn the rule publishes turn.status with every group member's messages and words in this step, which the AI moderator reads. Set the memory window (max_memory_events) to at least 40. Use it with a Discussion whose turns are set to procedure.

actions.description: Name who speaks next, or 'anyone' to leave the floor open.
When the floor is open: say privately whether you want to speak next.
The chosen participant posts a message (offered by the Discussion activity).

about.ends_when: When the configured number of turns has been taken, or nobody takes the open floor for the configured number of rounds in a row (unless 'End the step' is off).

max_turns.title: Group members' turns before the step ends (moderator messages do not count)

finish.title: End the step when the discussion is over

quiet_rounds.title: Quiet rounds before the step ends (nobody wants to speak)

about.summary: Always gives the floor to the group member who has said the least so far, a policy that balances participation without asking anyone.
about.how_it_works: At the start and after every turn the rule invites the group member with the fewest words in this step (discussion.invite); ties are broken at random with the run's seed, so it is reproducible. Participants whose role is 'moderator' are outside the group: they are never put in the rotation and are left out of the counts, and after each group member's message every moderator is asked privately whether it wants to speak next (turn.request); a yes gives it the next turn. After each turn the rule publishes turn.status with every group member's messages and words in this step, which the AI moderator reads. Use it with a Discussion whose turns are set to procedure.

actions.description: The invited member posts a message (offered by the Discussion activity).
Moderators only: say whether to step in before the next member.

about.ends_when: When the configured number of turns has been taken (unless 'End the step' is off).

max_turns.title: Group members' turns before the step ends (moderator messages do not count)

finish.title: End the step when the discussion is over

about.summary: Self-selection: before each turn everyone may privately raise a hand, and one of those who did gets the floor.
about.how_it_works: The first round asks every group member; moderators never open the discussion. Before each later turn the rule asks every participant except the last speaker, privately, whether they want to speak next (turn.request), so nobody sees the others' answers. Several raised hands is floor competition, recorded in turn.status as competitors: the member with the fewest words so far wins (or one at random with the run's seed). A moderator's raised hand always wins. If nobody raises a hand, the rule asks again, this time including the last speaker, who may go on; after the configured number of quiet rounds in a row the step ends. After each turn the rule publishes turn.status with every group member's messages and words in this step, which the AI moderator reads; moderators (role 'moderator') are left out of those counts. Every turn adds several actions, so allow enough actions per run and set the memory window (max_memory_events) to at least 40. Use it with a Discussion whose turns are set to procedure.

The chosen participant posts a message (offered by the Discussion activity).

about.ends_when: When the configured number of turns has been taken, or nobody wants to speak for the configured number of rounds in a row (unless 'End the step' is off).

about.summary: How evenly the group members contributed to the discussion, leaving moderators out, so groups with and without a moderator compare the same people.
about.how_it_works: Counts the discussion messages and their words of every participant whose role is not 'moderator', including members who said nothing. Evenness is the normalized entropy of the members' shares of words: 1 when everyone wrote the same amount, 0 when one person wrote everything.

outputs.label: Evenness
outputs.description: Normalized entropy of the group members' shares of words.

outputs.label: Details
outputs.description: Messages and words per group member, and the evenness of message counts.
